                  [32m'LANCEDB_URI = os.environ.get("LANCEDB_URI", "/app/lancedb_data")\n'[39m +
                  [32m'LANCEDB_TABLE = os.environ.get("LANCEDB_TABLE", "docs")\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'# Connect to LanceDB and open the table\n'[39m +
                  [32m'db = lancedb.connect(LANCEDB_URI)\n'[39m +
                  [32m'table = db.open_table(LANCEDB_TABLE)\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m"# Build a native LanceDB FTS index on the content column if it doesn't exist\n"[39m +
                  [32m'try:\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    has_fts = any(\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        getattr(idx, "index_type", None) == "FTS" and "content" in getattr(idx, "columns", [])\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        for idx in table.list_indices()\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    )\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    if not has_fts:\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        table.create_fts_index("content", use_tantivy=False, replace=False)\n'[39m +
                  [32m'except Exception as e:\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    # Fallback/safety: if the index already exists, we can ignore the error\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    if "already exists" not in str(e).lower():\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        raise\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'def expanded_search(query: str, k: int = 10) -> list[int]:\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    """\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    Perform full-text search with query expansion using WordNet synonyms.\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    \n'[39m +
                  [32m'    Parameters:\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    -----------\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    query : str\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        The user query string.\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    k : int, default 10\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        The number of top document IDs to return.\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        \n'[39m +
                  [32m'    Returns:\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    --------\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    list[int]\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        Top-k document IDs ordered by FTS score descending.\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    """\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    # Lowercase the query before expansion\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    query_lowered = query.lower()\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    \n'[39m +
                  [32m'    # Split the query by whitespace\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    tokens = query_lowered.split()\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    if not tokens:\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        return []\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        \n'[39m +
                  [32m'    expanded_terms = []\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    seen_all = set()\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    \n'[39m +
                  [32m'    for token in tokens:\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        # The original query term must remain in the expansion\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        if token not in seen_all:\n'[39m +
                  [32m'            seen_all.add(token)\n'[39m +
                  [32m'            expanded_terms.append(token)\n'[39m +
                  [32m'            \n'[39m +
                  [32m'        synonyms_for_token = []\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        seen_syns = set()\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        \n'[39m +
                  [32m'        # Look up WordNet synonyms\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        for synset in wn.synsets(token):\n'[39m +
                  [32m'            for lemma in synset.lemmas():\n'[39m +
                  [32m'                name = lemma.name().lower()\n'[39m +
                  [32m'                \n'[39m +
                  [32m"                # Only keep synonyms that are a single token (no '_' or whitespace)\n"[39m +
                  [32m'                if "_" in name or " " in name:\n'[39m +
                  [32m'                    continue\n'[39m +
                  [32m'                    \n'[39m +
                  [32m'                # Skip the original token itself\n'[39m +
                  [32m'                if name == token:\n'[39m +
                  [32m'                    continue\n'[39m +
                  [32m'                    \n'[39m +
                  [32m'                if name not in seen_syns:\n'[39m +
                  [32m'                    seen_syns.add(name)\n'[39m +
                  [32m'                    synonyms_for_token.append(name)\n'[39m +
                  [32m'                    if len(synonyms_for_token) == 3:\n'[39m +
                  [32m'                        break\n'[39m +
                  [32m'            if len(synonyms_for_token) == 3:\n'[39m +
                  [32m'                break\n'[39m +
                  [32m'                \n'[39m +
                  [32m'        # Add the synonyms to the expanded terms\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        for syn in synonyms_for_token:\n'[39m +
                  [32m'            if syn not in seen_all:\n'[39m +
                  [32m'                seen_all.add(syn)\n'[39m +
                  [32m'                expanded_terms.append(syn)\n'[39m +
                  [32m'                \n'[39m +
                  [32m'    # If no terms were expanded (should not happen since original tokens are kept), return empty\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    if not expanded_terms:\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        return []\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        \n'[39m +
                  [32m'    # Construct an OR/SHOULD boolean FTS query over the expansion\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    queries = [(Occur.SHOULD, MatchQuery(term, "content")) for term in expanded_terms]\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    boolean_query = BooleanQuery(queries=queries)\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    \n'[39m +
                  [32m'    # Execute the search and retrieve the top-k document IDs\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    results = table.search(boolean_query, query_type="fts").limit(k).to_list()\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    \n'[39m +
                  [32m'    # Return the top-k document IDs as a list of Python int\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    return [int(r["id"]) for r in results]\n'[39m +
                  [32m''[39m
